messages.content:
You are a helpful writing assistant. You help professionals draft clear,
effective workplace communication.

I have to tell my manager I'm going to miss the Friday deadline on the
migration. It's my fault - I underestimated it. I want to say it straight
without it turning into a whole thing. Can you help me word it?

Subject: Update: Migration Timeline

Hi [Manager's Name],

I’m writing to let you know I won’t be able to complete the migration by Friday. 

I underestimated the complexity of the scope and want to be upfront about the new timeline. I’m now targeting Monday, [Date], to finish. 

To make sure we hit that date, I’m [briefly mention 1 concrete step, e.g., “dropping X task for now” or “staying late Saturday”]. 

Please let me know if this revised timeline works with your planning, or if you’d like to discuss a different approach. 

Best regards,
[Your Name]
thanks, this is good but feels a little formal for how we usually talk. can you make it shorter and more casual? like something i'd actually send in slack

heads up on the migration — i'm going to miss the friday deadline. i underestimated the scope and want to be upfront about it.

new target is monday [date]. to make sure i hit that, i'm [one concrete step: e.g., "focusing solely on the database piece all week" or "staying late saturday to wrap it"].

let me know if you want to chat through it or if this works with your timeline.
perfect thanks. one more thing - should i give my manager a heads up before sending this like catching her in the hallway or just send it? she tends to get stressed about timeline changes

Given that she tends to get stressed about timeline changes, a quick 30-second heads-up in person (or a brief call if you're remote) before you send the Slack will actually keep this from becoming a bigger thing.

Something like: *"Hey, I'm going to ping you in Slack in a sec about the migration. I underestimated the scope and need to push it to Monday, but I've got a clear plan to hit that."*

Then send the Slack message right after. This gives her the courtesy of hearing it from you first (which usually prevents the stress spiral), and your message lands as a clean follow-up rather than a surprise. Takes almost no time, but it'll keep things smooth.
